transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Well, doctor, I... I came in because... well, it's since my grandson was killed. It's just been awful. I was sitting in the living room the other day, looking at the wallpaper—it's this lovely floral pattern I picked out back in 1982 when my husband was still alive, God rest his soul. We got it on sale at Sears, you know they used to have such wonderful sales. Anyway, my daughter was sitting right beside me, holding my hand. And I know I love her, I do. But... I just cannot feel the warmth of it inside me at all anymore. Just cold. Like the draft we used to get in the old house before we fixed the windows. Those windows were a nightmare to clean, let me tell you...
Have you found that you no longer take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like seeing your family or doing your favorite activities?

Yes, exactly like I was just saying. Since my grandson... since he was killed, my daughter can sit right beside me and hold my hand, and I know in my head that I love her, but I just can't feel the warmth of it inside me at all anymore. None of the good feelings are there. I used to feel so much joy when she'd come over. We used to bake pies together. Apple was her favorite, though I always preferred cherry. You have to get the tart cherries, though, not the sweet ones, or the filling turns out terribly mushy. I learned that from a magazine I used to subscribe to, Better Homes and Gardens, I think it was. The mailman used to deliver it every Tuesday. He was such a nice young man, always wore a hat, even in the summer heat... 

But... oh, what were you asking? Right, the pleasure. No, I just don't feel any of it anymore. Even when I try to do the things I used to love, it just feels empty.
Do you feel down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, since your grandson passed away?

Depressed? Well... no, I wouldn't say I feel sad or down in the dumps, not really. I don't sit around crying or anything like that. My neighbor, Martha, now she was depressed when her husband passed. Cried every single day. She used to buy those special aloe vera tissues by the case. You know the ones? They're supposed to be soft on your nose, but if you accidentally wipe your glasses with them, it leaves this awful greasy film. I told her, I said, 'Martha, you really shouldn't use those on your spectacles.' She wore those big plastic frames, the kind that were so popular back in the seventies. I had a tortoise shell pair myself, bought them at the optometrist downtown before they closed the shop and turned it into one of those fancy coffee places. I can't stand paying four dollars for a cup of plain black coffee, it's just highway robbery... 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right. No, I don't feel down or depressed like Martha did. I'm not crying all day. Like I said, I just don't feel much of anything at all.
